Healthcare Reform to Make America Great Again
Since March of 2010, the American people have had to suffer under the incredible economic burden of the Affordable Care Act—Obamacare. This legislation, passed along strictly partisan lines and mislabeled to hide its true ramifications, has to be repealed and replaced.
The Obamacare repeal and replace effort will be based on the following principles and reforms:
Completely repeal Obamacare. Our elected representatives must eliminate the individual mandate. No person should be required to buy insurance unless he or she wants to.
Modify existing law that inhibits the sale of health insurance across state lines. As long as the plan purchased complies with state requirements, any vendor ought to be able to offer insurance in any state. By allowing full competition in this market, insurance costs will go down and consumer satisfaction will go up.
Allow individuals to fully deduct health insurance premium payments from their tax returns under the current tax system. Businesses are allowed to take these deductions so why wouldn’t Congress allow individuals the same exemptions? This will make health insurance far more affordable for everyone.
Allow individuals to use Health Savings Accounts (HSAs). Contributions into HSAs should be tax-free and should be allowed to accumulate. These accounts would become part of the estate of the individual and could be passed on to heirs without fear of any death penalty. These plans should be free from government dictation and individuals should be able to use the money for routine health costs without penalty.
Require price transparency from all healthcare providers, especially doctors and health care organizations like clinics and hospitals. Individuals should be able to shop to find the best prices for procedures, exams or any other medical-related procedure. People should be able to know the cost before—not after—the service is provided.
Block-grant Medicaid to the states. Nearly every state already offers benefits beyond what is required in the current Medicaid structure. The state governments know their people best and can manage the administration of Medicaid far better without the one-size-fits-all Washington bureaucracy.
Remove barriers to entry into free markets for drug providers that offer safe, reliable and cheaper products. Congress will need the courage to step away from the FDA’s needless rules and restrictions that keep drug prices too high. We must also allow consumers access to imported, safe and dependable drugs from overseas that cost far less than here at home.
We must act quickly and decisively to repeal and replace Obamacare with free-market solutions that put patients and doctors—not Washington—back in charge of healthcare.
— Donald J. Trump
